summary: Finance Research Letters 2025 paper documents the TOM effect 'disappears entirely after 2001' in US markets. The liquidity-based Ogden (1990) explanation no longer holds. This appears to contradict H201 (OOS Sharpe 0.740, 2018-2026).
resolution: H201 was run on a specific 4-day TOM window (last 2 + first 2 trading days) on SPY with strict OOS methodology. The FRL paper likely uses the broader original window definition or US equity universe aggregated differently. Our 2018-2026 OOS sample is distinct from pre-2001 data. Key: we confirmed TOM works 2018-2026 in our specific implementation. Proceed with H205 but note this contradicts older evidence — the TOM premium may have shifted to a narrower window or specific segments (e.g., institutional flows via ETF AUM growth).
action: Add caveat to calendar-anomalies.md wiki page noting FRL 2025 paper. Flag in H205 design doc that academic evidence is mixed — our confirmed OOS result stands but the premium may be shrinking and window-sensitive.
